title: 1950 AHSME Problem 38
statement: If the expression \[ \begin{vmatrix}a&c\\d&b\end{vmatrix} \] has the value \(ab-cd\) for all values of \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d,\) then the equation \[ \begin{vmatrix}2x&1\\x&x\end{vmatrix}=3 \]

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: Is satisfied for only \(1\) value of \(x\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: Is satisfied for no values of \(x\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: Is satisfied for an infinite number of values of \(x\)

solutions.text:
The given rule turns the equation into \[ (2x)(x)-(1)(x)=3, \] or \(2x^2-x-3=0.\) Factoring gives \((2x-3)(x+1)=0,\) whose two distinct solutions are \(x=\tfrac32\) and \(x=-1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Apply the given rule to turn the determinant into a quadratic equation
